presetTiles.note: Grid measured from the artwork's own rules. Values are read off each tile: only preset 1 is configured on the captured machine, the rest are empty at 0.0 g / 60wpm.

zeroAdjust.note: Blue means selected and Start only zeroes what is selected. The menu opens with every weigh hopper selected and the dispersion pan not. Tapping a pan selects it individually (6.5); the weigh hoppers and the dispersion pan are never both selected, because 4.4.6 zeroes them as two separate operations.

feederAdjust.note: Operation Manual 6.12. Light the Time and/or AMP lamp key — the lamp goes green — then press Increase or Decrease to move the values of the selected pans. RF is per head; DF is the single dispersion feeder. The pans selected on Zero Adjustment are the same pans, so the selection carries.
feederAdjust.arrowNote: The Increase and Decrease keys are DIMMED in the artwork. They light only when there is something to move: a lamp key lit, and — on RF — at least one head selected.

rf.label: RF
rf.note: The grey RF arrow. Kept as a way back to the radial feeders; on the program the head numbers do that.

df.label: DF (the (1) under the DF bar)
df.note: Pressed on the running program: the (1) turns blue, a Target Wt key appears above Read OptimumVal, and Increase/Decrease move the DF values. Pressed again it clears; pressing a head number clears it too and picks that head.

bars.note: Measured off the running program: every RF head draws a navy Time bar and a magenta AMP bar, 1 px per unit (25.0 is 24 px tall, 50.0 is 49), on a baseline at y=380; the DF pair sits on its own baseline at y=248 and grew by exactly 1 px when Increase took 25.0/50.0 to 26.0/51.0.

rf.label: DF (the (1) on the disc)
rf.note: The (1) printed on the centre disc is the dispersion feeder's key: pressed on the original, the disc turns blue, the RF arrow reads DF, and the chart draws one circle per parameter. The grey RF arrow beside the chart is not a key.

unknownKeys.label: right arrow
unknownKeys.note: Does nothing. Pressed on the original with the power off and on, the machine running, and with no, one, two and all fourteen heads selected: no head changed, no value changed, the chart never moved. It also disappears in the bar-chart view, so it belongs to the radar artwork.

unknownKeys.label: left arrow
unknownKeys.note: Does nothing. Pressed on the original with the power off and on, the machine running, and with no, one, two and all fourteen heads selected: no head changed, no value changed, the chart never moved. It also disappears in the bar-chart view, so it belongs to the radar artwork.

run-feeder.wedgeNote: Head 1's wedge is baked blue in the capture, so a neutral base is generated with it greyed; the app tints up from that.

chart.note: Amplitude is the magenta trace. Measured off the capture: every head at 50.0 put it at r=61, so 100 sits at r=120, the ring's inner edge. Segment 1's arc is centred at 77 degrees, not at the bottom.

run-feeder.dfNote: With the dispersion feeder picked, a real CCW-R relabels the four keys along the top: DF Time, DF AMP, DF Weight (a lamp key) and Target Wt showing the DF target weight (photographed on a running machine, 2026-09-03). The Flash program this simulator is built from does NOT do this - its keys keep reading RF - so those four keys are drawn from the photograph, not captured.

feederAdjust.stepNote: One press of Increase or Decrease moves every lit parameter by 1.0, on every selected head — counted on the original, where RF Time went 25.0 to 26.0 on a single press.

dfTargetWt.note: The DF target weight: the amount of product the dispersion feeder is held at (the DF pan sits on its own load cell). Captured off the running program: the Target Wt key appears when the (1) under the DF bar is pressed, and opens a "DF Weight Setting" keypad reading 500, Maximum 9999, Minimum 1. Digits append to the shown value, as on the Entr keypad.

dfLimits.note: Entering the DF target weight is a three-step chain on the running program: Enter on DF Weight Setting opens "Upper Limit(%) Setting" (20, Maximum 100, Minimum 0), Enter on that opens "Lower Limit(%) Setting" (20, the same limits), and Enter on that returns to the screen. CANCEL on any step drops straight back to the screen.

hdrvParameter.note: Service 4.4.3.2.1: three hopper-drive parameter sets exist per unit, and the preset chooses which one the unit runs. The list was not captured (the header never opened under Ruffle), so it is drawn.
hdrvParameter.drawerNote: drawn from Service 4.4.3.2.1 — the open list was not captured

rows.label: IS-DS
rows.desc: Infeed signal to discharge: the delay from the packer asking for product to the weigh hoppers dumping it. Nothing lights on the cutaway; both tags go blue with an arrow beside them (seen on a running machine).

rows.label: IS-TH{n}
rows.desc: Infeed signal to the timing hopper: when the section's timing hopper opens after the request. C1 adjusts TH1, C2 adjusts TH2.

rows.label: IS-DTH{n}
rows.desc: Infeed signal to a diverting timing hopper. DTH1 and DTH2 belong to C1, DTH3 and DTH4 to C2; the radio under the table picks which one the row edits.

rows.label: IS-WH
rows.desc: Infeed signal to weigh hopper: the delay before the weigh hoppers open. Everything downstream is timed from the end of this. Only the IS tag lights (the program lit DS too; the machine does not).

rows.label: WH-PH
rows.desc: Weigh hopper to pool hopper: how long after the weigh hoppers open the pool hoppers refill them. Starts where IS-WH ends.

rows.label: PH-RF
rows.desc: Pool hopper to radial feeder: how long after the pool hoppers open the radial feeders run to refill them. Starts where WH-PH ends.

rows.label: STAGGER
rows.desc: Stagger: a spread between the weigh hoppers opening, so the product does not all land at once.

rows.label: WH-BH
rows.desc: Weigh hopper to booster hopper: how long after the weigh hoppers open the booster hoppers below them open. Starts where IS-WH ends.

rows.label: BH-WH
rows.desc: Booster hopper to weigh hopper: the delay before the weigh hoppers refill the boosters. Starts where WH-BH ends.

rows.label: WH ON
rows.desc: Weigh hopper open time. Starts where IS-WH ends - when the weigh hoppers open.

rows.label: BH ON
rows.desc: Booster hopper open time. Starts where WH-BH ends - when the boosters open.

rows.label: PH ON
rows.desc: Pool hopper open time. Starts where WH-PH ends - when the pool hoppers open.

bh.label: BH
bh.name: Booster hoppers
bh.note: Adds the WH-BH, BH-WH and BH ON rows, and a ring of booster hoppers under the weigh hoppers on the cutaway - the weigh-hopper ring cut from the capture and set one ring lower, lit the same way when a BH row is picked.

th.label: TH
th.name: Timing hopper
th.note: Adds the IS-TH row and makes the machine two sections: C1 (heads 1-8) adjusts TH1, C2 (heads 9-16) adjusts TH2.

dth.label: DTH
dth.name: Diverting timing hoppers
dth.note: Adds the IS-DTH row: DTH1 and DTH2 belong to C1, DTH3 and DTH4 to C2, and the radio under the table picks which one the row edits.

timingAdjust.note: From a running 16-head two-section machine with boosters and timing hoppers (IMG_7816, 2026-09-03) and the Flash program. The single arrows move the selected row by 10 ms and the double arrows by 100; a row at 0 goes no lower; Entr ("Time Input", Maximum 2550, Minimum 1, digits append) writes into the row. The bars are a timeline of delays: each interval starts where the ones before it end, so raising IS-WH slides every later bar right. The program's first row read WH-DS (Production: WH-PH); the machine's reads IS-DS, which is used here. The header follows the selected row.

bar.note: Measured off the Production capture: WH-DS 110 ms is 12 px, WH ON 450 is 40, PH ON 400 is 37 - about 0.09 px per ms, the column being wider than Preset's.
